clue.text: Georgia digs for the last of truffles with a wild flavour

parts.note: GA is the standard abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
digs as a verb means excavates, i.e. mines

indicators.note: the last of points to the closing letter of the next word only

explanation.surface: A truffle hunter in Georgia goes after the final few truffles with their strong, earthy taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaminess is the strong taste of game meat, a flavour reminiscent of wild creatures.

clue.text: Film on Aussie experts — they help keep the wheels of industry turning

definitions.text: they help keep the wheels of industry turning

parts.note: Grease is the 1978 musical film; also a thin film of grease
in Australian slang a gun is an expert, as in a gun shearer

explanation.surface: A movie about Australian specialists who keep factories running.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australian slang a gun is a top performer; 'on' just links, since in a down entry the second piece sits below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease guns force lubricant into machinery bearings, literally keeping industrial wheels turning.

clue.text: Opening strap up to show mandibles, say

parts.note: a mouth is an opening

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the next word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fastening a strap across an opening reveals an insect's jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouthparts are an insect's feeding organs, of which mandibles are an example.

clue.text: Ogden has nothing on this old Aussie conscript

parts.note: Ogden Nash was an American writer of comic verse
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: The poet Ogden Nash has nothing on a former Australian national serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'on' link: O sits on, after, NASH in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasho is Australian slang for a national serviceman, a conscript of the 1950s and 60s.

clue.text: Succumbing to pressure after secure, criminal occupation

indicators.note: after tells us the first-named piece comes second in the answer

parts.note: safe means secure
cracking means breaking down under stress

explanation.surface: Someone who felt safe starts to break down under the strain of a life of crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Safecracking, breaking into safes to steal, is a criminal trade or way of life.

clue.text: Psyching oneself up for a dance?

definitions.text: Psyching oneself up for a dance?

parts.words: Psyching oneself up for a dance?
parts.note: someone psyching themselves up might repeat 'I can, I can'; that repeated phrase is the name of a high-kicking French dance

explanation.surface: Someone nervously steels themselves before stepping onto the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a lively high-kicking French music-hall dance, whose name doubles the word for being able.

clue.text: These days it shows up in poetry — to do it pays, they say

definitions.text: to do it pays, they say

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the word for poetry

parts.note: verse is poetry

indicators.note: shows up in a down clue means the little word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Modern poems carry the old saying that it pays to promote yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows up' turns IT to TI, which goes 'in' VERSE. The definition completes the slogan 'It pays to advertise'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'it pays to advertise' says that promoting your wares brings profit.

clue.text: Dispatched, we hear, for very little money

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is chosen by how it is spoken

parts.note: dispatched means sent

explanation.surface: Sent off, as it were, for a pittance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cent is a hundredth of a dollar, a coin of very little value.

clue.text: Born and died in poverty

parts.note: née means born, used before a woman's maiden name
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone born and died poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Need means want or poverty, the lack of the means of living.

clue.text: Big Bird is to fly out to produce a milky substance

parts.note: the emu is a very large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the following words are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large bird is trying to take to the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal for the two short words. The surface joke is that an emu is flightless, so it can never take to the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulsify is to make an emulsion, a milky mixture of liquids that do not normally blend.

clue.text: No diamonds found in Venice — about time to get even?

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

indicators.note: No tells us to drop the diamonds from the city's name

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jewel thief finds no gems in Venice and wants revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes ICE from VENICE, leaving VEN; AGE goes 'about' it, giving A-VEN-GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to get revenge for it, so to get even with the wrongdoer.

clue.text: Company member takes on fishermen and financial officers

indicators.note: takes on means the following piece is attached after the first

parts.note: MP, member of Parliament
trollers fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat

explanation.surface: A company director hires some anglers and some accountants.
explanation.definitionFit: Comptrollers are officials who oversee accounts, financial controllers.

clue.text: Youthful singing group needs coach — nothing rich about it

parts.note: to coach someone is to school or train them

indicators.note: about signals that the following letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: O, the round zero, stands for nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A children's choir needs a coach, and the job is not well paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges O and RICH into CHOIR; 'it' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A school choir is a group of young pupils who sing together, a youthful singing group.

clue.text: Gamble about the maiden said to be a distraction

indicators.note: about means going round, so the gamble surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to dice is to gamble with dice

indicators.note: said signals that the word is represented by how it is spoken

parts.note: a maiden is a virgin

explanation.surface: A bet on a young woman proves a diversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives VERGEN, sounding like VIRGIN; DICE goes 'about' it, giving DI-VERGEN-CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Divergence is a turning aside from a course, so a deviation or distraction.

clue.text: Sets up professional bodies

definitions.meaning: to institute is to establish or set up
an institute is an organisation for a profession, such as engineers

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning establishes and a plural noun for learned or professional societies.

clue.text: Egg white imparts a dazzling shine, so they say

indicators.note: so they say signals that the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: glare is a harsh dazzling brightness

explanation.surface: Egg white gives a pastry a brilliant gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: Glair is a culinary and bookbinding term for egg white used as a glaze or adhesive.

clue.text: Castration's timeless remedy for what flashers use

indicators.note: remedy as a verb means to fix or put right, so the letters are reworked
timeless means the letter for time is removed from the word

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A doctor proposes castration as an instant cure for indecent exposure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' removes T (time) from CASTRATION, leaving CASRATION, which 'remedy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashers, people who expose themselves, traditionally wear raincoats to hide and reveal.

clue.text: A suitable vehicle for Kermit?

parts.note: Kermit the Frog lives on land and in water, so he would need a vehicle that can drive and float, which shares its name with the frog's animal class

explanation.surface: What car would a famous puppet frog drive?
explanation.definitionFit: An amphibious vehicle works on land and water, just as frogs are creatures of both.

clue.text: Coming back in take heart about English copper — he's unduly critical

indicators.note: coming back means the short word that follows is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means going round, so the heart surrounds the coin

parts.note: ticker is informal slang for the heart
P stands for penny, the English copper coin

explanation.surface: Someone takes courage around an English policeman while being excessively fault-finding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming back' turns IN to NI; TICKER goes 'about' P to give TPICKER. 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is a coin; 'take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitpicker fusses over tiny faults, a person who is unduly critical; the definition stands for the person.

clue.text: The first wife, not heartless, has an affair

parts.note: Eve was Adam's wife, the first woman in the Bible

indicators.note: heartless tells us to remove the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: The original wife cheats on her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the centre letter out of the printed word. 'Affair' suggests adultery after 'wife', but here it just means an occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occasion or happening, just as an affair can be a social function.

clue.text: A soft glow can please the student within

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: within means the student is placed inside the other word

parts.note: to please someone is to delight them
L for learner, from the L-plates of a learner driver

explanation.surface: A dim romantic glow can please the student inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts the learner inside the word for please, at its middle; L for learner comes from British L-plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlelight is the soft gentle light given off by burning candles.

clue.text: Watering place preferred by one on a diet?

definitions.meaning: a pub or nearby drinking spot where people go to drink

definitions.text: preferred by one on a diet?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., low in calories, which a dieter would choose

explanation.definitionFit: A local is British slang for one's nearby pub; split, it suggests low-calorie food.

clue.text: Potato in Christmas pudding?

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is found inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Is there a potato in the Christmas pudding?
explanation.walkthrough: Christmas pudding is the rich fruit pudding eaten at British Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is an informal word for a potato.

clue.text: Stain may be jam

definitions.meaning: to be in a jam, a tricky situation

explanation.definitionFit: Spot means both a mark and an awkward predicament, as in a tight spot.

clue.text: Tree in fashion, though not with upper crust

indicators.note: though not with means we drop a letter from the word for fashionable

parts.note: something in fashion is popular
U means upper-class, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U usage

explanation.surface: A tree is fashionable but not among the aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British label for upper-class speech and manners; dropping it from POPULAR leaves the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a tall fast-growing deciduous tree of the willow family.

clue.text: Flier about to hunt all over for something brown to eat

parts.note: a bee is a flying insect
C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: all over signals that the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bee searches everywhere for a brown snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' scrambles the hunting word. 'Flier' looks like a pilot or a leaflet but is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A beechnut is the small brown nut of the beech tree, which can be eaten.

clue.text: Dislike the journalist returning before the trial

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for the journalist is read backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the senior journalist
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Someone hates seeing a journalist come back ahead of a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to hate or strongly dislike something.

clue.text: Codicil changes liturgical books

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an addition to a letter, as a codicil is an addition to a will
alters means changes

explanation.surface: A supplement to a will amends the church's service books.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalters are books containing the psalms, used in church services.
